subject: brown hyena
title: On a Desert Beach, Hyenas Crack Seal Pups' Skulls With One Bite

scenes.text: In one African desert, the top predator hunts on the beach.
Brown hyenas on Namibia's southern coast live mostly on baby fur seals.
Seal remains turned up in about seven of every ten of their droppings.
A pup's skull hasn't hardened yet, so one crushing bite to the head is enough.
Some kills aren't even eaten. Others are buried in the sand for later.
A shy desert scavenger turned beach hunter. Its prey has flippers.

description:
On Namibia's southern Namib coast, near Luderitz, brown hyenas feed mainly on Cape fur seal pups.
A diet study found seal remains in about 71% of their droppings, and researchers watched them kill pups with a single bite into the still-soft skull. Some pups are killed and left, others cached for later. The Brown Hyena Research Project has followed these hyenas since 1995.
Which predator would you never expect on a beach?
first_comment: These hyenas have been studied on the same stretch of coast since 1995. Which animal would you least expect to find hunting on a beach?
